claims.text: Refractory oxide-forming elements such as Hf, Ta, or Cr can become enriched in oxide scales on multiprincipal-element alloys.
A continuous, self-healing protective oxide scale forms preferentially on a fine-grained, lattice-distorted matrix.
The protective oxide scale minimizes oxygen ingress and governs oxidation resistance and overall material integrity.
Inherent sluggish diffusion in the multiprincipal-element matrix suppresses deleterious elemental segregation.
Adding 0.5–1 at.% Hf is expected to enhance formation of a protective oxide.
Refining the grains is expected to improve protective-scale formation.
The governing structural mediator is a dense, adherent oxide scale formed along grain boundaries.
A high grain-boundary density facilitates formation of the protective scale.
Preferential surface enrichment of refractory oxide formers facilitates formation of the dense, adherent scale.
High lattice distortion impedes rapid elemental diffusion.
Impeded matrix diffusion prevents premature depletion of protective elements.
Grain boundaries act as rapid diffusion pathways for oxidizing species.
Grain boundaries act as nucleation sites for protective oxides.
Minute Hf additions improve scale continuity by forming refractory oxides with low oxygen permeability.
The cooperative action of grain refinement and refractory-element enrichment produces a self-healing scale that preserves mechanical integrity.
Relative to the baseline, the modified alloy or refined microstructure will form a thinner, more uniform, and more adherent oxide scale.
Relative to the baseline, the modified alloy or refined microstructure will exhibit lower oxidation mass gain.
Relative to the baseline, the modified alloy or refined microstructure will retain high-temperature hardness or strength better after oxidation.
Some baseline multiprincipal-element alloys can form nonprotective Mn oxides and undergo Mn depletion.
The proposed behavior should hold from approximately 700–900 °C for tens to 100 hours when oxidation kinetics are diffusion controlled.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome allows grain refinement alone to improve oxidation resistance, while the falsification rule says equivalent resistance from grain refinement alone would undermine the proposed combined effect. This makes the status of grain refinement as an independent sufficient intervention versus a required cooperative component ambiguous.
